The third season of the reimagined science fiction television series ''[[Battlestar Galactica (2004 TV series)|Battlestar Galactica]]'' premiered on [[Syfy|Sci Fi]] in the United States on October 6, 2006, and concluded on March 25, 2007. Unlike the previous season, it was not split into two parts and did not have an extended hiatus during the middle of the season. The third season contained 20 episodes.

==Production==
The Sci-Fi Channel ordered a 20-episode third season on November 16, 2005,<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2005/11/16/sci-fi-channel-charts-a-course-for-battlestar-galactica-season-3-19833/20051116scifi01/|title=Sci Fi Channel Charts a Course for 'Battlestar Galactica' Season 3|publisher=Sci-Fi Channel|date=November 16, 2005|access-date=July 2, 2011}}</ref> with production beginning in April 2006 in [[Vancouver|Vancouver, British Columbia]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2006/03/08/battlestar-galactica-returns-this-fall-20769/20060308scifi01/|title='Battlestar Galactica' Returns This Fall|publisher=Sci-Fi Channel|date=March 8, 2006|access-date=July 2, 2011}}</ref> The season premiered in the United States on October 6, 2006, in Canada the following day, and in the UK on January 9, 2007; with the first two episodes being shown together. The broadcast schedule for season three did not include a long hiatus in the middle of the season, as with season two. The Sci-Fi Channel moved the series to Sundays on January 21, 2007, the first time the show had changed nights since it began airing.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=May 20, 2008|url=https://www.variety.com/article/VR1117954313?refCatId=14|title=New 'Battlestar' orbit|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=November 20, 2006|last=Martin|first=Denise}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Critical response===
The season received universal acclaim from critics, scoring 94 out of 100 based on 14 reviews from [[Metacritic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/battlestar-galactica-2003/season-3|title=Battlestar Galactica (2003): Season 3|website=[[Metacritic]]|access-date=July 2, 2011}}</ref> On [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the season has an approval rating of 100% with an average score of 9 out of 10 based on 20 reviews. The website's critical consensus reads, "Dark, charming and unusually thoughtful, ''Battlestar Galactica''{{'}}s third season continues to improve on the show's most addictive elements."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/battlestar-galactica/s03 |title=Battlestar Galactica: Season 3 |website=Rotten Tomatoes |accessdate=November 12, 2021}}</ref>

The series also placed on numerous critics top ten lists of both 2006 and 2007 by publications such as the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'', ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'', ''[[Newsday]]'', ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[TV Guide]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2006/|title=Best TV Shows of 2006|publisher=Metacritic|access-date=July 2, 2011| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110714074830/http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2006/| archive-date= 14 July 2011 | url-status= live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2007/|title=Best TV Shows of 2007|publisher=Metacritic|access-date=July 2, 2011|archive-date=November 13, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081113131723/http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2007/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Accolades===
The third season received four [[Emmy Award]] nominations:<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2007/07/19/sci-fi-channel-scores-7-emmy-noms-including-writing-and-directing-nods-for-battlestar-galactica--25004/20070719scifi01/|title=Sci Fi Channel Scores 7 Emmy Noms Including Writing & Directing Nods for 'Battlestar Galactica'|publisher=Sci-Fi Channel|date=July 19, 2007|access-date=July 2, 2011}}</ref> Outstanding Writing for a Drama Series ([[Ronald D. Moore]] for "Occupation / Precipice"), Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series ([[Félix Enríquez Alcalá]] for "Exodus, Part 2"), Outstanding Sound Editing for a Series ("Exodus, Part 2"), and won for Outstanding Special Visual Effects for a Series for "Exodus, Part 2", the series' first Emmy win.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2007/09/08/winners-of-the-2007-primetime-creative-arts-emmy-awards-announced-25407/20070908atas01/|title=Winners of the 2007 Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards Announced|publisher=Academy of Television Arts & Sciences|date=September 8, 2007|access-date=July 2, 2011}}</ref> Ronald D. Moore was also nominated for a [[Writers Guild of America Award]] for Episodic Drama for "Occupation / Precipice".<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2006/12/13/2007-writers-guild-awards-television-and-radio-nominees-announced-23095/20061213wga01/|title=2007 Writers Guild Awards Television & Radio Nominees Announced|publisher=Writers Guild of America|date=December 13, 2006|access-date=July 2, 2011}}</ref>

==Home video releases==
The third season was released on DVD in region 1 on March 18, 2008,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-3-Menus/8860|title=Battlestar Galactica - 3rd Season Release Date MOVES! Plus a TON Of Menu Screen Previews, Too|publisher=TV Shows on DVD|first=David|last=Lambert|date=January 26, 2008|access-date=July 2, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100822235340/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-3-Menus/8860|archive-date=August 22, 2010}}</ref> in region 2 on September 3, 2007<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B000OY8NCE/|title=Battlestar Galactica: Season 3|publisher=Amazon.co.uk|access-date=July 2, 2011}}</ref> and in region 4 on November 20, 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ezydvd.com.au/item.zml/795624|title=Battlestar Galactica (2004) - Season 3|publisher=EzyDVD|access-date=July 2, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110303025914/http://www.ezydvd.com.au/item.zml/795624|archive-date=March 3, 2011}}</ref> It was also released on [[Blu-ray Disc]] in region 1 on July 27, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-3-Blu-ray/13742|title=Battlestar Galactica - Season 3 Blu-ray Disc Officially Announced: Date, Cost, Extras, Package|publisher=TV Shows on DVD|first=David|last=Lambert|date=May 11, 2010|access-date=July 2, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100819094750/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-3-Blu-ray/13742|archive-date=August 19, 2010}}</ref>

The sets include all 20 episodes from the third season, plus an extended 25-minute longer version of "Unfinished Business". Special features include creator [[Ronald D. Moore]]'s podcast commentaries for all 20 episodes. Actors [[Grace Park (actress)|Grace Park]] and [[Tahmoh Penikett]] join Moore for his podcast commentary on "Unfinished Business", and Moore's wife Terry Dresbach appears frequently throughout the podcasts as well. Moore also provides a new commentary track for the extended version of "Unfinished Business". Executive producer and writer [[David Eick]] provides commentary for "Hero". Bonus podcasts for the final three episodes are also included—writer [[Michael Angeli]] and actor [[Mark Sheppard]] on "The Son Also Rises" and Sheppard himself on both parts of "Crossroads". Also included is the ten-part webisode series ''[[Battlestar Galactica: The Resistance]]'', deleted scenes for various episodes, and 22 of David Eick's videoblogs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/32755/battlestar-galactica-season-three/|title=Battlestar Galactica - Season Three|publisher=DVD Talk|first=Todd|last=Douglass Jr.|date=March 24, 2008|access-date=July 2, 2011}}</ref>
